title: Transactional Outbox & Change Data Capture (CDC)
subtitle: Eliminating dual-write bugs between Postgres and Kafka
overview: Writing to Postgres AND publishing to Kafka in two separate network calls is one of the most common distributed data bugs: if the app crashes or Kafka blips between the two writes, your database and search/billing caches silently diverge. The Transactional Outbox + CDC pattern makes the state change and its event commit together, without distributed 2PC.
firstPrinciplesStory: Your Checkout Service runs `INSERT INTO orders ...` in Postgres, then calls `kafka.produce('OrderCreated')`. Everything looks great in staging until a pod OOM-kills right between the SQL `COMMIT` and the Kafka call—leaving a paid order in Postgres that Shipping and Billing NEVER hear about! Reversing the order fails too: publishing to Kafka before SQL commits lets Shipping mail items for orders that rolled back! Making the database WAL itself the single commit point solves both bugs cleanly.

adaptiveLenses.intuition: Instead of mailing a letter at the post office AND trying to update your checkbook separately (and dropping one if you trip on the stairs), you write BOTH the order AND the 'mail this receipt' slip on the exact same checkbook page in one transaction. A dedicated courier (Debezium CDC) reads your ledger's carbon copy (WAL) and guarantees every slip reaches Kafka.
adaptiveLenses.mechanics: Inside ONE local SQL transaction, app writes domain state (`orders`) AND appends an event row to an `outbox_events` table. Debezium tails Postgres's logical replication WAL (no polling load!) and streams `outbox_events` into Kafka partitions. Consumers deduplicate on `event_id` for effective-once sync.
adaptiveLenses.staffTradeoffs: CDC over WAL beats periodic `SELECT * FROM outbox WHERE sent=false` polling because WAL streaming adds near-zero query overhead and delivers sub-100ms propagation lag. Remember to periodically purge/partition processed outbox rows so the outbox table doesn't bloat—or truncate via Postgres `pg_logical_emit_message`.

ddiaAnchors.concept: Avoiding Dual-Write Race Conditions via Log Tail
ddiaAnchors.whyItMatters: Establishes one single system-of-record commit log that reliably feeds Elasticsearch, Redis, and downstream microservices.

pragmaticTips.tip: Never update two heterogeneous datastores via separate app-level network calls when consistency between them matters.
pragmaticTips.application: Derive search indexes, analytics, and domain events from one transactional WAL + Outbox.

keyTakeaways: App-level dual writes (`DB + Kafka`) always leave a crash window where one succeeds and the other fails.
Writing domain state + `outbox_events` inside one local ACID transaction makes emission atomic.
WAL-based CDC (Debezium) eliminates polling overhead and streams outbox events to Kafka with sub-100ms lag.

nodes.label: Order Service
nodes.summary: Inserts business row AND outbox row inside one atomic Postgres transaction.
failureModes: Publishing directly to Kafka inside app code causes silent dual-write drift

nodes.label: Postgres + Outbox Table
nodes.summary: Commits domain mutation + event atomically into the Write-Ahead Log.
failureModes: Unpruned outbox rows bloat disk unless periodically archived/deleted

nodes.label: Debezium CDC Relay
nodes.summary: Reads committed outbox inserts directly from Postgres WAL slot and routes to Kafka.
failureModes: Dropped consumer leaves inactive replication slot holding WAL disk space unless alerted

nodes.label: Kafka Event Bus
nodes.summary: Distributes guaranteed committed domain events to Search, Cache, and Billing.
failureModes: At-least-once CDC replay requires idempotent downstream consumers

nodes.label: Search & Billing Sinks
nodes.summary: Updates Elasticsearch and Billing projections idempotently via `event_id` / LSN.
failureModes: Out-of-order stale updates unless gated by LSN/version number

steps.info: BEGIN; INSERT orders(...); INSERT outbox_events(...); COMMIT;
steps.payloadInspector: Both domain state & outbox_events share the exact same ACID commit LSN=0/4A20B1
steps.inspectorNote: If the order rolls back, the outbox event rolls back too—zero phantom events!

steps.info: Debezium streams WAL record for outbox_events (0 SQL polling queries!)
steps.payloadInspector: WAL Logical Decode -> Table=outbox_events | EventID=evt_8841 | Aggregate=order_7
steps.inspectorNote: Logical replication streams only committed WAL changes sequentially.

steps.info: Debezium publishes OrderCreated to Kafka -> Search & Billing converge (eventually consistent, usually sub-second lag)
steps.payloadInspector: Topic: orders.events | Key: order_7 | Header x-event-id: evt_8841
steps.inspectorNote: Even if Kafka goes down for 10 minutes, Debezium pauses at its WAL offset and catches up cleanly when Kafka recovers.

predictPrompt.prompt: Why should downstream Search/Billing consumers check `event_id` (or LSN version) before applying a CDC message?
predictPrompt.hint: What happens if Debezium crashes right after publishing to Kafka but BEFORE saving its Connect offset?
predictPrompt.reveal: Debezium restarts from the last saved offset and re-emits `evt_8841` (at-least-once delivery). Consumers checking `event_id` or `version > current_version` guarantee zero duplicate processing or stale overwrites.

chaosScenarios.title: Kafka Cluster Outage During Checkout (Events Wait in the WAL)
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Kafka brokers become unreachable for 5 minutes while customers keep placing orders.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Checkouts keep succeeding because they only depend on Postgres; Debezium resumes from its replication-slot position once Kafka recovers.

steps.info: Orders + outbox_events persist safely in Postgres even while Kafka is unreachable
steps.payloadInspector: Checkout keeps succeeding; outbox_events rows and their WAL wait in Postgres
steps.inspectorNote: Notice the resilience gain: a downstream Kafka outage no longer takes down customer checkout!

steps.info: Kafka returns -> Debezium drains the 5-minute WAL backlog in order -> no committed event is lost
steps.payloadInspector: Resumed from replication slot LSN 0/4A20B1 -> synced all pending orders to Search & Billing
steps.inspectorNote: Committed orders stream to consumers automatically once Kafka is back. Keep a periodic reconciliation job anyway, as a safety net for consumer bugs or connector misconfiguration.

chaosScenarios.title: Debezium Down -> Replication Slot Pins WAL and Fills the Primary's Disk
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: The Debezium connector crashes on Friday night and nobody notices; its logical replication slot stays in place.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Alert on replication-slot lag in bytes, cap retention with max_slot_wal_keep_size (Postgres 13+), and restart or re-snapshot the connector before the disk fills.

steps.info: debezium_slot active=false -> Postgres must keep every WAL segment since its confirmed LSN
steps.payloadInspector: pg_replication_slots: slot=debezium_slot active=f retained_wal=180 GB | disk 92% used and rising
steps.inspectorNote: Checkout still works, so nothing looks wrong, until the primary runs out of disk and stops accepting writes.

steps.info: Alert fires at slot lag > 10 GB; max_slot_wal_keep_size=50GB bounds the worst case
steps.payloadInspector: SELECT slot_name, pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), confirmed_flush_lsn) FROM pg_replication_slots;
steps.inspectorNote: If the cap is hit, Postgres invalidates the slot to protect the primary; the connector then needs a fresh snapshot, which is slower but far better than a full disk.

pros: Zero polling load on primary SQL
Checkout works even if Kafka temporarily blips
cons: Adds Kafka Connect / Debezium operational component
Requires monitoring Postgres WAL replication slot retention
tradeoffs.bestFor: Orders, payments, search sync, microservices event-driven consistency

cons: Permanent silent divergence risk whenever crash/network fails between commits
